dimensions.definition: Personal care, emotional attachment or romantic feeling; separate from action
Voluntary ongoing personal bond distinct from professional cooperation
Romantic involvement; distinct from mutuality and from present relationship status
Belief another will act reliably or in good faith in a defined context
Recognition of someone’s skill, competence or courage
Approval of another’s principles, judgment or ethical character
Capacity to change someone’s decisions, whether or not formally empowered
Recognized formal authority within a defined structure or jurisdiction
Threats, intimidation, blackmail or force constraining someone’s choices
Reliance upon another for information, resources, protection or identity
Employment, legal partnership, colleagues or vocation-based tie
Teaching, training, guidance or protégé relationship
Biological, legal or acknowledged kinship; explicit nature required
Agreement or disagreement about ethics, means, ends, values
Joint action toward a goal in a specified circumstance
Opposition, combat, sabotage or active obstruction
Observed ability to coordinate despite differences; not identical to friendship
Taking action to shield another from harm
Violation of an established duty, trust, confidence or commitment

case_studies.title: Coercion is not authority
case_studies.observed: 1982 and 1988 clashes establish different views of lethal justice. A 2000 incident places Daredevil chained to a rooftop; a 2013 trial places Matt as a prosecution witness.
case_studies.interpreted: The relationship can be both a continuing moral confrontation and a constrained form of cooperation. The rooftop scene permits a hypothesis of coercive moral pressure.
case_studies.not_established: No direct evidence here that Frank has formal authority over Matt, that mutual moral respect exists, or that the encounter proves lasting personal hatred.

case_studies.title: Protective concern can coexist with rupture
case_studies.observed: Foggy offers Matt a role in the DA office; later ends their partnership amid concern about Matt’s stability. Matt helps conceal Foggy’s survival and, in another story, attempts to recover his soul.
case_studies.interpreted: An enduring bond can have context-specific breakdowns in professional trust without erasing affection or protection. Institutional power arises only in bounded official roles.
case_studies.not_established: We should not project the 2012 rupture across the entire history, or treat a job offer as proof that Foggy actually supervised Matt.

case_studies.title: Team cohesion is not friendship
case_studies.observed: Luke participates in a group seeking to contain the Shadowland crisis, then works alongside Daredevil and other Defenders during a later gang war.
case_studies.interpreted: Opposition in one historical context and collaboration in another are compatible; one involves resisting Matt’s conduct, the other coordinating against outside threats.
case_studies.not_established: These summaries alone do not establish private emotional closeness, deep personal trust, or that Luke recognized Matt’s authority outside a specific assignment.

case_studies.title: Trust is directional and historical
case_studies.observed: Elektra’s publisher synopsis calls Matt her most trusted ally during the Fist project and says she wants him as a partner.
case_studies.interpreted: The issue provides unusually strong source language for Elektra → Matt operational trust. It doesn’t automatically describe Matt → Elektra to the same degree.
case_studies.not_established: This is not evidence that Elektra has permanent authority over Matt or that their entire romantic history follows a single stable trust level.
